- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) and forecast is below recent low, adjust upward to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) and forecast is above recent high, adjust downward to avoid overestimating recovery.
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, reduce peak value and smooth transition to avoid overshoot.
- If forecast mean is consistently below true mean over 30d, apply upward bias correction, especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from negative to positive) within 5 days, adjust forecast to reflect momentum shift, not just historical mean.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, apply early correction bias toward sentiment direction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes, model should avoid overreacting to short-term volatility; apply dampening factor to forecast volatility.
